note: Literature confirms TBC1D32-related ciliopathy/syndromic hypopituitarism features hypopituitarism, midline craniofacial/pituitary anomalies, and polydactyly.

evidence.text: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in TBC1D32 were identified in siblings with panhypopituitarism and absent anterior pituitary, as well as a proband with growth hormone deficiency and anterior pituitary hypoplasia.

source.title: Loss-of-Function Variants in TBC1D32 Underlie Syndromic Hypopituitarism
source.quote: A Finnish family of 2 siblings with panhypopituitarism, absent anterior pituitary, and mild craniofacial dysmorphism, and a Pakistani family with a proband with growth hormone deficiency, anterior pituitary hypoplasia, and developmental delay.

numbers.metric: affected Pakistani probands with growth hormone deficiency

evidence.text: Recessive TBC1D32 mutations are characterized by polydactyly, hypopituitarism, and Joubert-like or pituitary anomalies on MRI, with literature reviews identifying facial dysmorphism and hypopituitarism as primary features.

source.title: Expanding the clinical and molecular spectrum of TBC1D32-related ciliopathy: case reports and literature Review
source.quote: A review of previously reported cases highlighted facial dysmorphism, retinal disease, and hypopituitarism as major clinical features of TBC1D32-related ciliopathy.

numbers.metric: newly reported unrelated patients with hypopituitarism and retinal disease
